That appears to be a snowball viburnum. My mother used to have one. Hers was huge. Taller than our house. They are similar in appearance to white hydrangea. Not the same family though. The viburnum do better in the sun, and are not cold tolerant. I could be wrong though, if that plant is located in the shade and/or in a northern clime. More likely to be a hydrangea then.

It looks like a snowball to me though. I have hydrangea, and the leaves and stems are slightly different.

With just this picture its hard to tell if its an old fashioned Snowball aka a white Annabella hydrangea, or a white viburnum.

 Both are very similar flowers with the viburunum having 5-8 inch flowering buds on a 6-10 foot plant. While the hydrangea has larger 8-12" buds on a 4-6 foot plant.

 The hydrangea also tends to bloom for a longer period of time than the vibrabium. But both are found in north america. Although the vibrabium. Is native to china, while the hydrangea is local.
